requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The one weak spot I found is symlinks, covered under Implementation.

## Implementation

**File discovery**
- `rust_files` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` walks the project root.
- It skips `.git` and `target` directories at any depth. It skips `book`, `evidence` and `vendor` only when the parent directory is the project root, which matches the requirement.
- Directory, entry and file-type errors are reported rather than silently dropped.
- One edge case: symlinked `.rs` files are not followed, because `entry.file_type()` does not follow symlinks. I treated this as negligible.

**Parsing and parse failures**
- `validate_rust_functions` reads each file and calls `missing_function_references`. That calls `outline::parse_with(&RUST_PROFILE, …)`, which runs `check_errors` and rejects any tree with error or missing nodes.
- The failure is reported as `file:line: cannot parse Rust source: …`. Unreadable files are reported too, so no file is skipped silently.

**Which items are checked**
- The Rust profile in `src/outline/rust.rs` maps `function_item` and `function_signature_item` to `fn`. That covers free functions, methods, trait methods without bodies, nested functions and test helpers.
- It also maps `struct_item`, `enum_item` and `union_item`.
- `missing_function_references` keeps only the kinds `fn`, `struct`, `enum` and `union`, and reports `(declaration_line, kind, name)`.
- `validate_rust_functions` formats this as `file:line: kind name has no requirement or example citation`, so file, line, kind and name are all reported.

**Which references count**
- Comment ownership comes from the outline's `assign_comments`, which implements `outline_comments`. That requirement is assessed separately; here I only check that this code uses it.
- Only comments from `outline.comments` and fenced comment blocks from `comment_fences` are consulted. String literals, enclosing `mod` or `impl` comments, and evidence inputs therefore cannot count.
- The Rust profile's `comment_binds_to_container` handles inner doc comments. Attributes and outer doc comments attach to the item.
- `counts` rejects Term references, so a reference to a term does not count.
- A reference to a built-in counts only when `builtin.check(kind, fenced)` accepts it. For example, `habeas:none` must be a fenced `{cite}` with a non-empty justification.
- Unclosed fences are ignored.
- A reference to an example counts only if `example_references_requirement` finds a `{cite}` or `{test}` of a real requirement in the example.
- Unknown names do not count.

**Reporting and marking**
- `inspect_repository_with_progress` in `src/evidence.rs` calls the validator and folds its errors into the report. That function and the other functions I reviewed carry `{impl}` markers: `rust_files`, `display_path`, `validate_rust_functions`, `missing_function_references`, `example_references_requirement` and `OutlineNode::display_name`.
- I found no behavior in the implementing code that the requirement does not specify.

## Tests

**Unit tests in `src/rust_coverage.rs`**
- `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers:
  - enclosing `mod` and `impl` comments not counting;
  - references in plain and raw string literals not counting;
  - an unknown requirement name;
  - body comments counting;
  - a comment run across a blank line;
  - a trailing comment not leaking to the next item;
  - an inner doc comment binding to its `mod`;
  - an outer doc comment counting.
- `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, nested functions, `#[test]` functions, test helpers, and `{test}` on an example.
- `an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement` covers examples that:
  - cite a requirement;
  - are tested against a requirement;
  - have no requirement;
  - only chain to another example;
  - only cite a term;
  - plus a plain `{impl}` of a term.
- `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` covers:
  - struct, enum and union;
  - a reference before an attribute or field inside the item;
  - a reference before a variant;
  - a nested struct.
- `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` covers:
  - exclusion of `target` and `.git` at any depth;
  - exclusion of `book`, `evidence` and `vendor` at the root only (`src/vendor`, `src/book` and `src/evidence` are still checked);
  - a parse failure being reported.
- `locates_functions_after_unicode_text` checks line locations after non-ASCII text.

**Integration tests**
- `tests/references.rs` covers fenced `habeas:none` in its valid, inline, empty, wrong-role, unknown-built-in and unclosed forms.
- `tests/commands.rs` checks that `status` surfaces Rust findings in every form.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs` checks that a Rust parse failure fails the batch before configuration is loaded.

Symlinks and filesystem read errors are not tested, which I judged acceptable given how little they matter.

There are no FIXME-acknowledged gaps.

Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} no_requirement
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this only when no requirement or example applies to the item under the
> reference procedure. The citation MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST
> justify why the item exists. An item with an invariant worth checking, such as
> a cache that must not change results, needs a requirement stating that
> invariant instead. An item citing this MUST NOT implement end-user-observable
> behavior that no requirement specifies.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it. Validation MUST report an inline citation of it
or a fenced citation whose body, without comment delimiters and other
references, is empty. Whether the justification holds MUST be assessed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. `habeas status --all` MUST list
each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
